The Anse Trabaud report was read in selected sections. Its 600 to 1200 study interval is approximate; preliminary plant identifications and environmental interpretations remain qualified. No claim of eating poisonous manchineel fruit is made.
The 2007 ceramics report was read through its indexed Saint-Pierre excerpt. No complete volume review or independent inspection of the collection is claimed.
The 22 May uprising and 23 May 1848 abolition proclamation are distinct. Official overviews that collapse them to one date are not followed.
The 1802 to 1848 period describes continuity of slavery, not uninterrupted French sovereignty. British occupations are not treated as emancipations.
Tropiques is discussed through Hel-Bongo’s original literary study. The journal’s complete run was not independently read; interpretation is attributed.

The December 2015 installation is supported by the local biodiversity observatory and the historical legal version. A ministry summary’s 1 January 2016 formulation is not used to date the first meeting.
The overseas archives date the department law to 19 March 1946. Césaire’s parliamentary index is used for his report and named questions, not as proof that policy goals were achieved.
No named conqueror or successor map link is invented. A current French island is not an independent nation or the Grenadian island of Petite Martinique.
Independent historical review, depth certification and full geometry review remain pending.
